title: Count-conserving state-distinct capability-compute frontier
question: For the registered persistent-state retrieval workload, what is the minimum fraction of states reranked that preserves at least 80% of exhaustive reference capability under a state-distinct downstream task?
hypothesis: Increasing factor granularity reduces candidate occupancy, while increasing factor beam recovers coverage. A count-conserving pooled-success analysis should expose the capability/computation frontier without ratio averaging or truncation artifacts.

endpoints.name: capability_retention
endpoints.role: primary capability-constrained frontier endpoint; min(1, summed selective successes / summed exhaustive successes)

decision_rule.condition: For every M/configuration, sum integer exhaustive and selective success counts across seed cells and compute one capability_retention scalar from those sums. A configuration is eligible exactly when that stored scalar is >= 0.80.
decision_rule.licenses: a registered capability-constrained frontier on the corrected state-distinct workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: a universal optimum, universal sublinear retrieval, or hardware wall-clock speedup

decision_rule.condition: At each M, report the eligible configuration minimizing states_scored_over_M. Also identify fixed configurations eligible at all three M levels and report the one minimizing mean states_scored_over_M.
decision_rule.licenses: per-M and fixed-configuration capability/computation frontier evidence on this workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: general semantic addressing or a completed C5 proof

held_constant: same 48 training codes versus 16 held-out target codes
same task seed stream across arms
predecessor_3: TACOSM-C5-COVERAGE-FRONTIER-003 (VOID: truncation of pooled success counts)
protocol_note: The scientific search surface is unchanged. This registration changes only the aggregation implementation: success counts and evaluation counts are summed exactly across seed cells, and all capability/eligibility quantities derive from those exact totals.

result_note.interpretation: Supports a bounded capability-constrained sparse retrieval frontier on the registered synthetic workload. The fixed 16/6 configuration preserves at least 85.2% of exhaustive reference capability across all tested M while reranking about 15.1% of the state population on average. This does not establish sublinear asymptotic scaling, universal semantic retrieval, or hardware speedup. Absolute exhaustive capability falls from 36.2% at M=128 to 5.4% at M=512, so retention is relative to a weak reference ceiling at large M.
